gold_question: The news subscription service system operates as follows: The system allows users to subscribe to news via email. News information includes News ID and News Name. Subscription information includes Subscription Status, Creation Time, Modification Time, and the IP Address at the time of subscription. Users can update their subscription status or cancel their subscription at any time based on their needs.

The database schema named 'rschema_0381' contains three tables: 'User', 'News', and 'Subscription'.
The 'User' table represents a user entity, with columns for 'Name' (a string of up to 255 characters) and 'User_ID' (an integer primary key).
The 'News' table represents a news entity, with columns for 'News_ID' (an integer primary key) and 'News_Name' (a string of up to 255 characters).
The 'Subscription' table represents a subscription relationship between users and news, with columns for 'Creation_Time', 'Modification_Time', 'News_ID' (an integer not null, referencing the 'News' table), 'Subscription_IP' (a string of up to 255 characters), 'Subscription_Status' (a string of up to 255 characters), and 'User_ID' (an integer not null, referencing the 'User' table). Both 'User_ID' and 'News_ID' together form the primary key of this table.
The 'News_ID' and 'User_ID' columns are foreign keys referencing the 'News' and 'User' tables respectively, ensuring referential integrity. The 'News_ID' and 'User_ID' columns cannot be null, thus maintaining entity integrity. The 'Subscription_Status' column allows null values, and has no default value, maintaining domain integrity.
